correctness.rationale: The exact tangent section radius rho_t(z)=(t-z)/sqrt(t²-1), the Hausdorff support bound |s_t-t/2|<=d, and the bounded orthogonal-cylinder body D_d yield explicit positive lower and upper inclusions for the Steiner-centered overlap, converging to the 1/2-dilate of D_d. Symmetry plus Brunn--Minkowski bounds the intersection of arbitrary cylinder translates by vol(D_d), while backward sqrt(t) shifts yield a feasible intersection converging to D_d. This proves numerator and denominator limits for all d>=2. A standalone standard-library verifier checked the planar Steiner formula and rigorous finite-t bounds; it is not a replacement for the analytic proof.

originality.rationale: Feldman (arXiv:2608.04516v1) proves the analogous planar 4/9 bound for aligning centroids, and explicitly asks in Question 20 whether a better rigid-motion selector exists, suggesting the Steiner point. The source’s cone construction uses centroid recentering; it does not give the n-orthogonal-spike Steiner-selector 2^{-n} limit. The classical Steiner integral and central symmetry/Brunn--Minkowski ingredients do not, without the derived cross-section and translation bounds, imply the new sharp asymptotic witness. Relevant indexed claims concern centroid cores, product centroid bounds or unrelated selector objectives. Web literature searches for Steiner-point overlap comparisons found no equivalent; unindexed classical prior work remains possible.

value.rationale: A 2026 convex-geometry paper explicitly poses optimization over selector rules and identifies the Steiner point as a natural candidate. This theorem settles an important negative comparison: on a two-body planar family, Steiner alignment has efficiency tending to exactly 1/4 while centroid alignment has a 4/9 universal worst-case guarantee. The dimension-uniform orthogonal-cylinder limit and quantitative bound provide structural content beyond a numerical counterexample. It does not claim the global unrestricted Steiner constant.
